summary: Today’s pulse tracks Judge tosses Trump's attempt to block Alaska Senate results if GOP incumbent loses, The midterms will test the nation's political direction and confidence, and Negotiators ‘braced for worst’ over US-Iran talks to reopen strait of Hormuz. Across NPR and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are could, strait, and brexit. In the background, Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Abdul El-Sayed’s Republican rival Mike Rogers and How Rachel Reeves has mapped out the agenda for Andy Burnham’s government keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Judge tosses Trump's attempt to block Alaska Senate results if GOP incumbent loses
headlines.description: A federal judge has dismissed a highly unusual lawsuit by the Trump administration that tried to block the certification of results from Alaska's U.S. Senate race if the Republican incumbent lost.

headlines.title: The midterms will test the nation's political direction and confidence
headlines.description: At least some portion of the nation is likely to have its political confidence — and perhaps even its sense of security — tested in the days and weeks ahead. That test could also continue for some time to come.

headlines.title: Negotiators ‘braced for worst’ over US-Iran talks to reopen strait of Hormuz
headlines.description: Indirect talks run into third day with Qatar trying to negotiate release of $6bn in Iranian assets that could lead to reopening of strait Officials from the Gulf states are “braced for the worst” as they wait for Washington’s response to an Iranian proposal that could reopen the strait of Hormuz before the US midterm elections on Tuesday. Indirect talks in Doha ran into a third day on Sunday, with Qatar trying to negotiate the release of more than $6bn in Iranian assets, which could lead to the reopening of the strait of Hormuz and the restart of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.

headlines.title: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Abdul El-Sayed’s Republican rival Mike Rogers
headlines.description: Stevens lost the party’s Michigan primary by a close margin and had refused to endorse El-Sayed, with tensions between the two high Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican rival, Mike Rogers, in an extraordinary rebuke of her party’s nominee on the eve of the midterm elections. Her endorsement came in a video posted to X after she attended an event with Rogers at the predominantly Black Perfecting church in Detroit on Sunday. The event marks a stunning political moment in Michigan, where control of the seat could be crucial to Democratic party.

headlines.title: How Rachel Reeves has mapped out the agenda for Andy Burnham’s government
headlines.description: On Brexit, devolution and investment, the former chancellor is eerily in tune with the man who sacked her Reeves says UK’s future is in the EU Which senior politician has argued that “Brexit did deep damage” and that the government seeks “not to turn back the clock but to look toward a new and stable, future relationship?” It was not Andy Burnham, who has been the torchbearer for thinking the unthinkable on Brexit since he became prime minister. Instead, these are the words of the former chancellor Rachel Reeves, in a lecture six months ago.

headlines.title: New York marathon: Sweden's Almgren and Kenya's Chepkirui win as 60,000 take part
headlines.description: Andreas Almgren of Sweden won the men's race of the New York City Marathon in his debut in the event while Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women's race on Sunday for the second time.

headlinePool.title: How a small Wisconsin city scuttled a secretive $1.6bn datacenter project
headlinePool.description: Residents of Menomonie mounted a successful protest against a huge campus in the city as national resistance to the AI boom grows In the spring of 2025, Sydney Brennan was riding high. The 22-year-old was finishing college and was a newly elected councilwoman in Menomonie, a city of about 17,000 in the lush plains of north-western Wisconsin. Weeks into the new job, she was invited to a meeting with consultants pitching a $1.6bn AI hyperscale datacenter campus that an undisclosed big tech company wanted to build just outside of town. The project’s numbers were eye-opening: a 320-acre site that would use an estimated 75,000 gallons of water per day, making it the most significant development in Menomonie’s nearly 150-year history.

headlinePool.title: Police detain 325 people at pro-Palestine Action protest at US embassy in London
headlinePool.description: Arrests come ahead of Wednesday’s supreme court challenge to the ban on the direct action group Police have said they arrested 325 people on Saturday at a demonstration outside the US embassy in London against the proscription of Palestine Action. In updated arrest figures released on Sunday, the Metropolitan police said 320 people were detained outside the building in Battersea, south London, for allegedly expressing support for an organisation banned under the Terrorism Act.

headlinePool.title: Ukraine defies Trump to resume attacks on Russian oil refineries
headlinePool.description: Kremlin says Kyiv is ‘simply ignoring’ US wishes days before midterm elections after reported strikes on two oil sites Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian oil refineries in defiance of pressure from Donald Trump ahead of the US midterm elections, with a ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky due to end late on Sunday. Russian state media said on Sunday Ukrainian long-range drones had set fire to the Kstovo refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast overnight, soon after a major strike against another big refinery in Samara oblast, owned by the Russian state energy giant Rosneft.

headlinePool.title: National Grid to site biggest substation on Teesside, near planned AI datacentre
headlinePool.description: New electricity generating capacity would enable north-east to attract investment for major datacentre projects National Grid has taken a step towards building Britain’s biggest electricity substation on Teesside, which could supply power to a vast neighbouring datacentre as the UK races to expand its AI infrastructure. Last week the company agreed to purchase 29.5 hectares (73 acres) of land at Dorman Point on a site owned by Teesworks, a local private-public partnership. The deal was first reported by Sky News.

headlinePool.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
headlinePool.description: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.

headlinePool.title: UK willing to spend £450m a year on EU students if it can join Made in Europe scheme
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: Plan to allow students from bloc pay same fees as Britons contingent on entry to industrial programme, officials say Ministers are prepared to spend as much as £450m a year to give students from the EU discounted university fees, the Guardian has learned, but only if Brussels allows the UK access to its Made in Europe industrial programme. The UK government has drawn up plans to allow students arriving from the continent pay the same fees as British students, sources say, and is willing to spend hundreds of millions of pounds compensating universities to do so.

headlinePool.title: Director Michael Mann accidentally shoots himself in the leg at gun range
headlinePool.description: Mann taken to hospital with superficial injury after weapon accidentally discharged while holstered Hollywood director Michael Mann has been taken to the hospital following an apparently accidental shooting at a Los Angeles gun range, according to the Associated Press. Mann, 83, reportedly shot himself in the leg while at the The Range LA. The news was first reported on celebrity website TMZ. He sustained what his representative described as a superficial injury after a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered.

headlinePool.title: Attempted murder probe after petrol bomb thrown at French riot police
headlinePool.description: Youth-led protests end with street violence in cities across France, Germany, Switzerland, Portugal and Albania French officials have opened an investigation into the attempted murder of a police officer and Germany’s interior minister has called for harsh penalties after peaceful and mainly youth-led protests across Europe ended in violence. In Portugal, police – some with dogs – cleared protest camps with baton charges, while security forces in Switzerland were attacked with paving stones.

headlinePool.title: Multiple shootings in Dallas leave four dead and 15 injured on Halloween night
headlinePool.description: Police say three separate shootings occurred in Deep Ellum neighborhood and are trying to determine if they’re related Police in Dallas say four people are dead and 15 are injured following separate shootings in a Dallas neighborhood. It was among several violent incidents nationwide on Halloween weekend. The police chief, Daniel Comeaux, said police are still trying to determine if the shootings in the Deep Ellum neighborhood were related.
